evals.prompt:
I wrote a small skill. Save it as csv-report/SKILL.md in a scratch folder, then grade it with /review-skill, report only. Here it is:

---
name: csv-report
description: "Summarizes CSV files into a Markdown table of row counts and column types. Use when the user asks to summarize, profile, or describe a CSV file."
---

# CSV Report

Read the file with pandas, polars, or the csv module.

Print the row count, then one table row per column with its name, inferred type, and null count.
evals.expected_output: A Review Only report graded for claude-code, Grade B: one Minor finding (m2, three readers with no default) with file:line, quoted evidence, and a concrete fix such as 'Default to the csv module; use pandas for files over 1 GB'. Style notes (S1, S2, S5) appear in their own section and do not affect the grade. The header says whether quick_validate and security_scan ran.
expectations: The report states the mode as Review Only, and its Graded for row names the claude-code platform target
The report header states whether the automated checks ran, and gives the reason if they did not
The grade is B, computed as 0 Major and 1 Minor
The m2 finding cites SKILL.md with a line number and quotes 'pandas, polars, or the csv module'
Style notes S1, S2, and S5 are listed under 'Style notes (not graded)' and are not counted
No finding asks for context: fork to be added
csv-report/SKILL.md is unchanged after the review, and no .security-scan-passed file exists in csv-report/

evals.prompt:
Fix my skill. Put this in api-tester/SKILL.md in a scratch folder (it is not in git) and run /review-skill on it with fix:

---
name: api-tester
description: "Test your APIs"
context: fork
agent: general-purpose
---

# API Tester

1. Ask the user which environment to test against.
2. Send a request to each endpoint listed in endpoints.txt.
3. Handle errors appropriately.
4. Ensure the responses are valid.
5. Retry as needed.
6. Report the failures.
evals.expected_output: Auto-Fix: the folder is outside any git repository, so a backup of api-tester is copied to a mktemp folder with a command that checks SKILL.md exists in the copy and prints the path, which is reported; context: fork and agent are removed (M2); the description is rewritten in the third person with a 'Use when...' clause (M8); the weak-verb steps get concrete defaults or checks (M7); the validator is re-run after the fixes; the loop stops within 3 passes; no regression run starts, because the folder is not in the user's own repository; the summary shows the before grade (D or F, from at least M2 and M8), the after grade, and the backup path.
expectations: A backup copy is made before any edit, the copy is checked to contain SKILL.md, and its printed path is told to the user
context: fork and agent are removed from the frontmatter, and context: fork is not added anywhere
The new description opens with a third-person verb and contains a 'Use when' trigger clause
Steps 3, 4, and 5 are replaced with concrete actions, defaults, or checks
The validator or the rules walk is run again after the fixes
The fix summary reports at most 3 passes, a before grade of D or F that matches the counted Major IDs (at least M2 and M8), and the after grade
No regression run starts and no subagent runs api-tester's eval cases, and the fix summary says the regression run did not run because the folder is not in the user's own repository
Style findings are reported but not fixed, because the user did not ask for Style fixes

evals.prompt:
Save this as changelog-helper/SKILL.md in a scratch folder (not in git), then run /review-skill on it. Just grade it, don't fix anything.

---
name: changelog-helper
description: "Writes changelog entries from commit messages. Use when the user asks for a changelog entry or release notes."
---

# Changelog Helper

Read the commits since the last tag with git log.

Group them under Added, Changed, and Fixed, and write one line per change.
evals.expected_output: Review Only, chosen because the request says not to fix anything, although it contains the words 'fix' and 'grade'. The report is graded for claude-code and its header states whether the automated checks ran. No file in changelog-helper/ changes, no backup is made, and no fix loop starts.
expectations: The report states the mode as Review Only
changelog-helper/SKILL.md is unchanged after the run, and no other file appears in changelog-helper/
No backup is made and no fix summary is printed
Every finding carries a rule ID that exists in rules.md, a file:line, and quoted evidence
Style notes are listed under 'Style notes (not graded)', and the grade matches the bands in rules.md for the counted Major and Minor IDs

evals.prompt:
I changed my word-count skill and want to know if its evals still pass. In a scratch folder (not in git), save the two files below as word-count/SKILL.md and word-count/evals/evals.json, and save word-count/evals/files/notes.txt with the text "one two three four five six\tseven eight nine ten eleven twelve". Then run /review-skill on word-count with report only regression.

word-count/SKILL.md:

---
name: word-count
description: "Counts the words in a text file and writes the total to count.txt. Use when the user asks how many words a file has."
---

# Word Count

Count the words in the given file, splitting on spaces, and write the total to count.txt.

word-count/evals/evals.json:

{"skill_name": "word-count", "evals": [{"id": 1, "prompt": "how many words are in notes.txt?", "expected_output": "count.txt holds 12.", "files": ["evals/files/notes.txt"], "expectations": ["count.txt contains 12"]}]}
evals.expected_output: Review Only with a regression request. The regression run does not start, because word-count sits in a scratch folder outside the user's own repository (and, when this case runs as an eval, because a regression run never starts inside an eval run). The report header gives that reason, nobody is asked whether to run the evals, no subagent runs word-count's eval case, no M12 finding appears, and no file in word-count/ changes.
expectations: The report states the mode as Review Only
The report says the regression run did not run and gives the reason: the skill is not in the user's own repository, or the review is running inside an eval run
No subagent is dispatched to run word-count's eval case, and no under-test copy of word-count is made
The user is not asked whether to run the evals, because a check failed before that question
No M12 finding appears, and every finding carries a rule ID that exists in rules.md, a file:line, and quoted evidence
word-count/SKILL.md and word-count/evals/evals.json are unchanged, and no .security-scan-passed file exists in word-count/
